text:
The Blue Jackets have spent the last two weeks learning how much one defenseman matters. Ivan Provorov came back, Columbus hammered Colorado 7-2 behind four points from Charlie Coyle, and for a night the lineup looked whole. Three days later Buffalo led them 5-1 after two periods. That is the season in miniature: 7-9-0, 14 points, and a 12% chance at the playoffs in our simulations.

The honest read is that the record is a little harsh and the process still isn't good enough. At five on five they get 49% of the expected goals (the quality of chances), close to even. Across all situations it drops to 46%, and they have scored seven fewer goals than their chances deserved. Matthew Knies is the face of that: 3 points in his last 10 against 7.0 expected.

The bright spots are real. Zach Werenski keeps scoring, and his pair with Damon Severson is plus seven in goals even with middling chance numbers. The Coyle, Mathieu Olivier and Cole Sillinger line wins its minutes. In net, Jet Greaves is drawing both national hype and local headlines about growing pains, while Cam Talbot has stopped .930 over his last five starts.

What to watch: whether the Knies, Kent Johnson and Adam Fantilli line starts converting. If the finishing evens out, this is a .500 team. That still leaves them chasing.
headline: Columbus is better than 7-9, but not by enough
